newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Nesher Israel Cement invests $180 mln in dry line.
newsitem.headline: Nesher Israel Cement invests $180 mln in dry line.

text.p: Nesher Israel Cement Enterprises Ltd will invest $180 million in a new dry production line at its plant in Ramle, near Tel Aviv, company officials announced on Sunday.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Industry and Trade Minister Natan Sharansky will attend a cornerstone laying ceremony at the Ramle plant later on Sunday.
The output of the new production line, to be completed in two-and-a-half years, will be 5,000 tonnes a day.
Nesher, Israel's cement monopoly, is jointly owned by Koor Industries and Clal Industries, two of the country's largest holding companies.
Besides Ramle, Nesher has a plant in the town of Nesher outside Haifa and another near Jerusalem.
Nesher chairman Joseph Rosen said the building of the new production line would employ more than 1,000 workers directly for the next two and a half years.
The new production line brings Nesher's total investments this decade to more than $700 million.
Rosen said the dry production line, the second at Nesher's Ramle plant, was part of a strategic plan to replace all of the company's wet lines at Ramle and Nesher by 2001.
The Nesher plant, which operates three production lines based on the wet system and three cement mills, produces two million tonnes of cement a year.
The Ramle factory has three production lines based on the wet system and one dry line as well as five cement mills. The plant produces four million tonnes of cement annually.
The third site, outside of Jerusalem, produces one million tonnes of cement. It has one production line based on the half dry system and two cement mills.
Rosen said the new dry line will make production more efficient, replace the need for importing primary materials and reduce the costs of production as well as of the end product.
Nesher president and chief executive Yitzhak Davidi said the company was preparing to build another dry line at the Nesher plant near Haifa.
